title: DNA binding study of antifungal drug Ketoconazole by molecular docking and spectroscopic analysis.
authors: Ozkul, Mustafa Alp; Akgul, Tunahan; Bozaslan, Mehmet Serif; Toksoy, Suleyman Can; Dikmen, Gokhan
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
one_liner_zh: 该文通过光谱实验和分子对接研究抗真菌药物酮康唑与ct-DNA的小沟槽结合，属于广义蛋白质-DNA互作（实为小分子-DNA）且含分子对接方法，但对象非TF-DNA体系，深度有限。
abstract: The process of developing new drug molecules is long-term, costly, and especially the process of moving to clinical trials takes a long time. Consequently, conducting experimental and theoretical binding studies of drugs or drug candidates with biological materials, such as DNA and RNA, are crucial to reduce costs and minimize time requirements. As the DNA a fundamental biological molecule constitutes a major target for numerous pharmaceuticals, binding studies of various molecules with DNA is a broad field of research. DNA binding properties of antifungal drugs are of great importance in understanding their biological activities and elucidating their mechanisms of action. DNA binding studies also provide critical information to optimize the effects of antifungal drugs on target cells and to increase the selective toxicity of drugs. Ketoconazole (KTZ) is an azole-containing antifungal drug, and azole-containing drugs have many pharmacological properties. In this study, the interaction between the KTZ molecule and calf-thymus DNA (ct-DNA) was examined using various spectroscopic methods. The binding constant between ct-DNA and KTZ molecule was calculated using results obtained from different spectroscopic methods. UV-vis and fluorescence studies indicated a binding constant was calculated as 5.8 x 10(4) M(-1) and 6.21 x 10(4) M(-1) for the interaction between KTZ and ct-DNA, respectively. ct-DNA quenched the fluorescence of KTZ with a quenching constant approximately equal to 13 x 10(12) M(-1).s(-1). Fluorescence displacement experiments using ethidium bromide (EB) and Hoechst 33,258 revealed interaction between KTZ and ct-DNA occurred through minor groove binding mode. This conclusion was further supported by viscosity measurements, DNA melting studies, and KI quenching experiments. In light of experimental results, KTZ molecule quenches the fluorescence of DNA with a static mechanism due to the negative values of thermodynamic parameters such as DeltaH(o) and DeltaS(o). In addition, the interaction of the KTZ molecule with ct-DNA was investigated theoretically by Molecular Docking. It interacts with the minor groove of DNA through a combination of van der Waals forces and hydrogen bonding interactions.
abstract_zh: 开发新药物分子的过程是长期且昂贵的，尤其是进入临床试验阶段耗时漫长。因此，对药物或候选药物与生物材料（如DNA和RNA）进行实验和理论结合研究，对于降低成本、缩短时间至关重要。由于DNA作为基本生物分子，是众多药物的主要靶点，各种分子与DNA的结合研究是一个广泛的研究领域。抗真菌药物的DNA结合特性对于理解其生物活性和阐明其作用机制具有重要意义。DNA结合研究还为优化抗真菌药物对靶细胞的效果及提高药物的选择性毒性提供了关键信息。酮康唑（KTZ）是一种含唑类抗真菌药物，而含唑类药物具有多种药理特性。本研究采用多种光谱方法考察了KTZ分子与小牛胸腺DNA（ct-DNA）之间的相互作用。利用不同光谱方法获得的结果计算了ct-DNA与KTZ分子之间的结合常数。紫外-可见光谱和荧光研究表明，KTZ与ct-DNA相互作用的结合常数分别为5.8 x 10(4) M(-1)和6.21 x 10(4) M(-1)。ct-DNA以约13 x 10(12) M(-1).s(-1)的猝灭常数猝灭了KTZ的荧光。使用溴化乙锭（EB）和Hoechst 33,258的荧光置换实验表明，KTZ与ct-DNA之间的相互作用通过小沟结合模式发生。这一结论进一步得到粘度测量、DNA熔解研究和KI猝灭实验的支持。根据实验结果，由于热力学参数如DeltaH(o)和DeltaS(o)为负值，KTZ分子通过静态机制猝灭DNA的荧光。此外，通过分子对接 (molecular docking) 对KTZ分子与ct-DNA的相互作用进行了理论研究。它通过范德华力和氢键相互作用的组合与DNA的小沟结合。
